sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Province of Alberta, Canada (provincial incorporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; federal CBCA regime not elected for this entity)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (Federal State with dual federal-provincial legislative competence)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–China Agreement for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA, 2012, in force 2014)
Canada–Hong Kong Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (2016)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP, 2018)
Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, 2017)
Canada–China Income Tax Agreement (1986, as amended) and Canada–Hong Kong Income Tax Agreement (2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 2.1, 22.2, 23.1 (Individuals with Significant Control register); Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.3; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), SC 2017, c 21; FINTRAC guidance under the PCMLTFA.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport and proof of residential address of each ultimate beneficial owner / individual with significant control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Notary in the document origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada acceded effective 2024-01-11); Consular Legalization through Global Affairs Canada or the Canadian consulate where the origin jurisdiction is not a Hague Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Corporate Status of each direct or indirect corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague jurisdictions, Consular Legalization plus sworn English translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and Officers of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent or corporate secretary of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for each UBO or corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank of the UBO or corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and apostilled / consularized as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney / corporate resolution authorizing the Canadian legal representative to file pre-incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin or board of directors of the corporate shareholder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against: (a) FINTRAC and Criminal Code s 462.3 prescribed persons; (b) the UN Consolidated List implemented under the United Nations Act; (c) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List maintained by Global Affairs Canada under SEMA and the Magnitsky Law; (d) domestic and foreign PEP registers; (e) FATF high-risk jurisdiction notices. Obtain notarized identification, proof of address, source of funds/wealth statements, and bank references before engagement; apply enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk geographic origins. OFAC screening is not statutorily imposed in Canada but is applied contractually by Canadian financial intermediaries for SWIFT wire and Alibaba Pay onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry; mandatory NUANS name search report must be procured from an accredited NUANS service provider
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must use Roman characters of the English or French alphabet; the NUANS report must cover both linguistic forms. Names may include numerals, punctuation, and the mandatory legal element 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.' or 'Incorporated'. Non-Roman script trade names (e.g., Chinese brand marks) must be transliterated into Roman characters for the registered corporate name and may be additionally protected as an extra-provincial trade name or trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Loan, Insurance, Assurance, Broker, Investment Dealer
Engineer, Engineering, Architect, Lawyer, Legal, Barrister, Notary
Royal, Crown, Government, Canada, Alberta (when implying royal, federal, or provincial patronage)
Corporation, Ltd., Inc., Co. (misleading legal element combinations)
Municipal, Police, RCMP, Commission, Board (as a government body)
Hospital, Pharmacy, Doctor (when implying regulated professional services)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, obtain a fresh NUANS report incorporating the rejected name variant and file a written name-approval review with the Registrar of Corporations at Service Alberta, including legal submissions, trademark certificates, and a letter of consent from the holder of any conflicting name. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, incorporate under a new distinctive element or apply for judicial review to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Alberta Rules of Court. All re-filings must occur within the 90-day NUANS validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible. Alberta law requires a registered office with a full street address in Alberta (a post office box alone is insufficient) and a registered records address for service of process. For this B2B cross-border wholesale platform with no physical storefront, a licensed virtual office / registered agent address is accepted, provided the agent maintains business hours and statutory records in Alberta. For CRA commercial substance, management and control should be exercisable in Canada, and a Canadian bank account should be maintained for SWIFT and Alibaba Pay settlement flows.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — estimated annual probability below 5%. Alberta Corporate Registry does not conduct routine on-site inspections of registered office addresses; CRA and FINTRAC supervision for this low-risk e-commerce activity is documentary. Unannounced physical inspections are not applicable to registered offices of an ISIC 4791 electronic marketplace absent regulatory triggers.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: ISED-accredited NUANS service provider / Service Alberta
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory accreditation tariff; prevailing market fee CAD 40–50

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Articles of Incorporation filing fee under the Alberta Business Corporations Act
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Registrar of Corporations, Service Alberta)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee per Service Alberta fee schedule (approximately CAD 350)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO / Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register drafting and initial ownership records
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Canadian corporate and AML legal counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market flat fee for ABCA ISC compliance setup

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate minute book, organizational resolutions, and share certificates
Registered office and registered records address service (first year)
Notarization and apostille / consular legalization of the UBO document bundle (per set)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public in origin jurisdiction and Global Affairs Canada / consular authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document prevailing statutory and notarial fees, variable by jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Director consents, pre-incorporation statutory declarations, and start-up filing preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat fee; no separate statutory filing fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT compliance review for SWIFT wire and Alibaba Pay payment rail onboarding
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; aligned to PCMLTFA, payment-rail KYC, and OFAC-conditional contract requirements

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA); ss. 8-15 (incorporation and articles), s. 101 (registered office), s. 106 (directors), s. 110 (officers), s. 102 (corporate records)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Corporate Registration System (Service Alberta, Edmonton, Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 03 - Articles of Incorporation (filed electronically under s. 8(3) ABCA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the ABCA; nominal subscription consideration acceptable; no escrow account or capital deposit requirement; non-resident shareholding permitted without restriction
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION - DATED ______. 1. Ratification: RESOLVED that the Articles of Incorporation filed with the Alberta Corporate Registry on ______, File No. ______, be and are hereby ratified and approved. 2. Registered Office: RESOLVED that the registered office is fixed at [address], Alberta, in accordance with the Notice of Registered Office. 3. Share Subscription: RESOLVED that the subscription shares be allotted and issued to the incorporator for $1.00 per share, per the Articles. 4. Officers: RESOLVED that [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each serving at the Board's pleasure. 5. Banking: RESOLVED that the President and Treasurer may open bank accounts and sign banking documents. DATED ______, 20____.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Approval and NUANS Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (via accredited NUANS Search Houses or Corporate Access portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary online name availability check; order a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) report through an accredited search house; select a distinctive corporate name reflecting the B2B marketplace business or elect a numbered company; the NUANS report is valid for 90 days from issue; the proposed name must be distinguishable from existing Alberta and federal corporate names and registered trademarks.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and business purpose description
Contact details of the incorporator and intended directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on distinctiveness or similarity grounds, file a written consent of the senior user, add a distinguishing element (e.g. geographic descriptor or distinctive initials), or adopt a numbered company; resubmission within the NUANS validity window carries no additional search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry - Corporate Registration System (online) or Registry Operations, Edmonton
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 03 (Articles of Incorporation) specifying the corporate name, registered office address, classes and maximum number of shares, first directors, and any restrictions on business; attach the valid NUANS report; pay the CAD 275 (approx. USD 200) filing fee; electronic filing issues the Certificate of Incorporation immediately upon approval, while paper filing is processed within approximately 5 business days.
required_dossiers: Form 08 - Consents to Act as Director (where filed with the articles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a Request for Correction, rectify the flagged deficiencies (e.g. share class drafting, director residential address declarations) and resubmit the corrected Articles; resubmission within 30 days is exempt from a second filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry - Corporate Registration System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 04 (Notice of Registered Office) and Form 05 (Notice of Directors) promptly after incorporation, either simultaneously with the Articles or immediately following the issue of the Certificate of Incorporation; director names, addresses, and residency declarations must match the Articles; maintain the registered office as the statutory address for service of process and corporate records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (as retrieved from the Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects the notices due to missing director consent or incomplete addresses, file Form 08 consent or a corrected notice; a nominal late-filing correction fee (not exceeding CAD 100) applies under the ABCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registration (CRA Business Number)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online; Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration (TRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register online with the CRA to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN); open the corporate income tax account (T2), the GST/HST account (5% federal GST; Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax), and the payroll deductions account (RP) if hiring employees; provide the Certificate of Incorporation, registered office address, and director particulars; the BN serves as the single tax identification number for both CRA and Alberta corporate tax purposes.
required_dossiers: Directors' names, residential addresses and dates of birth
First fiscal year-end date and fiscal period election
Banking details (optional, for refund direct deposit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the online registration is rejected on a data mismatch, contact CRA Business Enquiries at 1-800-959-5525 to reconcile the profile or submit Form RC59 (Business Consent) requesting a correction to the BN account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary or City of Edmonton - Business Licensing / Planning Services (municipal bylaw authority)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Business Licence under the applicable Municipal Business Licensing Bylaw for the activity 'electronic commerce / online marketplace operation'; submit corporate information (legal name, BN, registered office address) and evidence of zoning compliance for the principal physical office; a fire safety inspection may be required if an office or storage area is occupied; the licence must be displayed at the principal place of business.
required_dossiers: Lease or proof of premises and zoning compliance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality refuses the licence on zoning grounds, apply for a discretionary use approval or minor variance with the planning department, relocate to a permitted office zone, or appeal the refusal to the municipal subdivision and development appeal board within 21 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Records, Minute Book and Share Certificate Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Office (corporate secretary or registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the statutory corporate minute book containing the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles, Notices, first board resolution, register of directors, register of shareholders, share certificate book and general ledger; issue share certificates evidencing the subscription shares; maintain the registers at the registered office as required by ABCA s. 102; adopt the initial corporate bylaws in accordance with the first board resolution.
required_dossiers: Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors
Minutes of the First Board Resolution
Share certificate forms and statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a share certificate or register entry is defective, the board may pass a supplemental resolution to cancel and reissue the certificate; lost certificates are cured by an indemnity bond and duplicate issuance; annual return obligations remain ongoing corporation compliance items.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to ISIC 4791 (electronic B2B wholesale platform operation); no industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over the purely digital service model; advisory oversight rests with Alberta Ministry of Jobs, Economy and Trade
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial industrial or manufacturing operating permit required; the sole operational authorization is the municipal Business Licence issued under the applicable City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Business Licensing Bylaw

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) - Environmental Assessment Program, under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12 (EPEA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class Exempt - the activity is not listed in the Mandatory and Exempted Activities Regulation (A.R. 204/2021); no environmental impact assessment or registration is triggered for an office-based digital marketplace without physical manufacturing units or stationary emission points
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater or VOC discharge; applicable thresholds: Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives (AAAQO) for any standby generators; municipal wastewater effluent limits under the City of Calgary or City of Edmonton Wastewater Bylaws; electronic waste and battery disposal per Alberta Recycling Management Authority guidelines and EPEA hazardous waste handling rules (A.R. 347/1990)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate and building occupancy permit issued under the Safety Codes Act (Alberta) and Fire Prevention Act (Alberta); structural load inspection for office floor capacity, server racks, and storage areas; workplace occupational health and safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (Alberta) and the OHS Code, including first-aid equipment, fire exits and emergency evacuation planning

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); digital portal: My Business Account via https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html; Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA on behalf of Alberta under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity obtains a statutory Business Number (BN) by: (1) registering online through CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO) portal or submitting paper Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number); (2) creating the applicable program accounts (RT for GST/HST, RC for payroll, RP for corporation income tax); (3) for non-residents operating through a Canadian digital distribution platform, GST/HST registration is required where taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold or where the platform is deemed to make supplies in Canada under the July 1, 2021 e-commerce framework; (4) the BN is generally issued within 5-10 business days for online filings; (5) a separate Alberta corporate income tax account is not required because Alberta's corporate income tax is collected federally.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box regime; a Business Corporation incorporated in Canada is a resident corporation taxed under ITA Part I on worldwide income. Available statutory elections include: (1) GST/HST annual filing and quick-method elections for qualifying small suppliers; (2) ITA section 85 rollover election for tax-deferred transfers of property to a corporation; (3) elections under ITA ss. 216/216.1 for non-residents to file on a net basis for Canadian-source rental and service income; (4) hybrid mismatch rules under ITA ss. 18.4-18.7 apply with mandatory adjustment rather than elective opt-out; (5) for entities fiscally transparent in a foreign jurisdiction, Canada determines classification by domestic law, with no mirror election, and treaty/domestic characterization governs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST - Federal Goods and Services Tax (Excise Tax Act, Part IX); Alberta has no provincial sales tax, therefore only the 5% federal GST applies in Alberta.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies over the trailing four consecutive calendar quarters (small-supplier exemption); non-resident digital platform operators and sellers of taxable goods/services through a Canadian distribution platform are deemed to make taxable supplies in Canada and may be required to register regardless of a Canadian physical establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance regime, no mandatory e-invoicing, and no digital stamping or API clearance requirements. The CRA does not pre-authorize invoices; taxpayers must retain all electronic and paper sales and export records for six years, and any e-invoices must be accessible in readable format. Suppliers must display their GST/HST registration number on invoices, and B2B platform operators must maintain auditable transaction trails for supplies facilitated in Canada.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act applies to: (a) tangible personal property exported from Canada by the supplier or at the supplier's direction within 60 days of delivery, supported by satisfactory export evidence; (b) services supplied to a non-resident person where the service is not performed in Canada or, if performed in Canada, is not in respect of Canadian real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of performance; and (c) intangible personal property (including platform access, software, and marketplace listing or intermediation services) supplied to a non-resident for use wholly outside Canada. A B2B cross-border marketplace platform supplying listing, subscription, or commission-based intermediation services to non-resident merchants is generally eligible as a zero-rated supply of services to a non-resident under Sch. VI Part V, s. 7, unless the service relates to real property in Canada or to goods situated in Canada when the service is performed.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (electronic filing via CBSA's Canadian Export Reporting System or Form B13A) for goods valued above CAD 2,000 or controlled/prohibited goods
Commercial invoice or sales contract evidencing the sale and export obligation
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the carrier naming the Canadian supplier and the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/SWIFT wire confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Cargo control documents or destination-country customs entry documentation where available
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits zero-rating claims by requiring proof of actual export and receipt of payment. Failure to maintain satisfactory books and export evidence results in reassessment at 5% GST, plus arrears interest and penalties. Knowingly false statements or gross negligence attract a penalty under ETA s. 285 of the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the tax understated, and exposing the exporter to ITA s. 163(2) gross-negligence penalties (50% of understated income tax). CRA may reassess beyond the normal four-year period where misrepresentation is attributable to neglect, carelessness, or willful default. Export proceeds are expected to be repatriated within 180 days of shipment as a commercial and documentary norm; failure to repatriate does not automatically claw back zero-rating, but it weakens commercial substance in subsequent audit challenges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (the monetary authority and fiscal agent for the Government of Canada); foreign exchange administration lies with the Department of Finance (Canada) through the Exchange Fund Account. Canada maintains no standalone foreign-exchange-control authority, and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) regulates federally chartered banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has full current and capital account convertibility under IMF Article VIII. There are no surrender, licensing, or prior-authorization requirements for inward or outward capital transfers. Profit remittances (dividends, management fees, royalties, interest) are freely repatriable, subject to Part XIII non-resident withholding tax, which may be reduced under the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) or an applicable tax treaty, and subject to supporting transfer-pricing and corporate-documentation requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export proceeds in Canada. Exporters may retain foreign currency balances in Canadian or offshore accounts without surrender; however, all international electronic funds transfers (EFTs) and incoming/outgoing wire transfers of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported to FINTRAC and are subject to AML/KYC documentation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium: Canada does not have an Electronic-Money-Institution licensing framework. Fintech cross-border payment providers (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, or similar) generally operate as money-service businesses registered with FINTRAC rather than as banks; they are acceptable for low-risk operational collections and disbursements, but they cannot legally hold client funds as a deposit-taking escrow account. Capital escrow and treasury settlement should be maintained with a Schedule I or Schedule II chartered bank operating in Canada.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence in a bank branch is not an absolute statutory requirement for directors; remote onboarding using certified digital identity, video verification, and electronic signatures is commonly accepted by Canadian banks. However, for non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners, many Tier 1 banks require a recorded video interview and may demand a physical visit for high-risk source-of-funds or if the corporate register shows shareholder opacity. A Canadian resident signatory or second authorised officer is strongly recommended to expedite account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) opacity or chain of custody that does not reveal all natural persons holding 25% or more of voting equity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta Corporate Registry certified corporate profile; full organisational chart; notarised UBO declaration; government-issued photo ID and proof of residential address for each natural person; shareholder register; board resolution confirming UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border B2B transaction flows indicating high transaction velocity, large denomination payments, or mismatches between expected customer base and the stated wholesale platform activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan and use-of-funds narrative; executed supplier agreements and customer onboarding policies; sample invoices and purchase orders; logistics and warehousing documentation; platform transaction dashboard exports; third-party audit trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipt of funds from high-risk jurisdictions or payment intermediaries not subject to equivalent AML supervision
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and adverse-media screening results; counterparty bank and intermediary information (bank name, SWIFT BIC); underlying commercial contracts; source-of-wealth evidence; confirmation that funds are not derived from shell corporate structures; legal opinion from Canadian counsel on trade sanctions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Detection of politically exposed persons (PEPs) among directors, UBOs, or beneficial owners in decision-making roles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP declaration and detailed position/reference explainer; source-of-funds documentation; independent professional introduction letter from a Canadian legal or accounting firm; enhanced due diligence questionnaire confirming no public-office abuse, plus corroborating corporate registry records and media searches.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection from a non-resident parent into the Canadian corporate treasury is executed via SWIFT MT103 with standard international remittance purpose codes: 'EQUI' (equity injection), 'LOAN' (intercompany loan), or 'EXTR' (capital account credit) as required by the receiving bank. The bank must receive a board resolution approving the injection, a subscription agreement or loan agreement, source-of-funds documentation, and a beneficial owner certificate. Settlement is made through the Canadian large-value payment system Lynx (RTGS) or same-day ACH under Payments Canada rules; all wire amounts equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000 are reported to FINTRAC, and the transaction is recorded as a direct investment with Statistics Canada under the CPA program if thresholds are met.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for the B2B marketplace use: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier and cross-border platform disbursements; (ii) commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 and confirmed by a Canadian clearing bank for larger bulk-import orders; and (iii) CAD and USD wire transfers through RTGS Lynx and CHIPS/ACH correspondent hubs. For Chinese suppliers, a dual-track rail is available using either standard USD SWIFT clearing or cross-border RMB (CNH) through CIPS with the onboarding bank maintaining a RMB correspondent account; for domestic Canadian vendors, payments execute via Payments Canada (E-mail Money Transfer for low-value items, or EFT/ACH for batch disbursements). All outgoing transfers require a supporting commercial invoice, underlying contract, and export/proceeds documentation under the bank's trade-finance controls.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Canadian-dollar FX forwards (standard forward contracts and forward-swaps)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CAD permissible where settlement in CAD is impracticable
Cross-currency swaps between CAD, USD, CNY, EUR, and other trade currencies
FX vanilla options (puts, calls, and zero-cost collars)
Currency interest-rate swaps and FX swap agreements

stage_5.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) — CORES portal
stage_5.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation or amalgamation; must be filed every calendar year
stage_5.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty CAD 100 (~USD 73) if filed after the due date; sustained delinquency exposes the corporation to administrative dissolution/cancellation by the Registrar (typically after 5 consecutive years of default); directors face good-standing and enforcement consequences.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined standard headline rate for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) located in Alberta: 15% federal general corporate rate plus 8% Alberta provincial general corporate rate (Alberta rate held at 8% since the 2019-2020 reduction schedule was paused).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction (SBD): the first C$500,000 of active business income of a CCPC is taxed at a combined 11% (9% federal + 2% Alberta small business rate). SBD access is restricted once taxable capital employed in Canada exceeds C$10M and is fully clawed back at C$15M (associated corporations share the C$500,000 limit via T2 Schedule 9). Alberta imposes no capital tax and no payroll tax. No sector-specific tax holiday applies to electronic wholesale platform operators; ordinary deductions (e.g., salaries, SaaS costs, platform commissions, bad debts, CCA on servers/software) apply.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return — filed through the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) T2 E-file system (engines: EFILE via approved tax software, or GIFI schedules submitted on the Corporation Internet Filing portal; hard-copy T2 accepted only below the C$1M gross-revenue electronic-filing threshold).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (each fiscal period ending within the calendar year; corporate income tax instalments are due monthly or quarterly on the 15th during the year and the balance-due is calculated at year-end).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 must be filed within 6 months after the fiscal period end. The balance-due date is 2 months after the fiscal period end for most corporations; a CCPC that is eligible for the SBD (and whose taxable capital phase-out does not preclude it) gets 3 months after the fiscal period end to pay.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Page 1 – Identification (name, Business Number, RC account, fiscal period end)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Canadian corporation, its 15-digit Business Number (BN) (assigned by the CRA when the Canada Revenue Agency account is opened or upon federal incorporation), the fiscal period end date, and the province of residence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the BN issued to the Alberta/federal corporation; if the entity is non-resident-owned, indicate the 'NR' tax account numbers and the branch/fiscal period key; non-resident directors do not require a Canadian SIN — the corporation's BN serves as the filing key.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 1 – Net Income (per GIFI Schedule 126 income-statement codes)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue (digital platform commissions, subscription fees, payment-routing fees), cost of goods/services sold, deductible operating expenses, and net income before tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenues attributable to a permanent establishment in Canada are included; foreign e-commerce turnover not attributable to Canada is excluded; a transfer-priced commission paid to the related non-resident operator must be supported by s.247 documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (Schedule 1, line 150) minus net capital-loss carryovers and non-capital loss carryovers claimed, with adjustments for dividends received (s.112 deductions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-capital losses of up to 20 prior years may be deducted; if the corporation has C$1M+ non-arm's-length transactions with the Chinese operator, attach the contemporaneous documentation summary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Line 250 – Canadian tax payable with Schedules 5 and estimate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of federal (net of abatement and general rate reduction) and Alberta provincial tax (8% general / 2% SBD) on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Alberta component is due to Alberta (via the T2 provincial tax return); a non-resident corporation otherwise taxable in Alberta must still file the T2 and may be entitled to the same provincial SBD only if it is a CCPC (rare) — otherwise the general 8% rate applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 9 – Related and Associated Corporations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List of all associated CCPCs and their taxable capital / ABI, used to allocate the SBD business limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Chinese parent and any Chinese-affiliated corporations that control the Alberta corporation count as associated/related to the extent of control in fact — full disclosure prevents reassessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing (s.162(1)): 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay, to a maximum of 12 months. Repeat failure within 3 years (s.162(2)): 10% plus 2% per full month, maximum 20 months. Arrears interest: CRA prescribed rate (base T-bill rate + 4%) compounded daily accruing from the balance-due date. Failure to file information schedules (e.g., Schedule 50 – shareholder information) and gross-negligence penalties (s.163) of 50% of the understated tax can be stacked.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T106 Information Return – Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents (electronic T106 via the CRA's Internet filing or approved software; must accompany the T2 reporting period).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, covering all transactions with non-arm's length non-residents in the fiscal period.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the same date as the T2 (6 months after the fiscal period end); unreported related-party flows are treated as undisclosed transfer-pricing positions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer name/BN and the non-resident related party (Chinese operator / Shanghai entity) identification, country of residence, and relationship code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must identify the beneficial owner and the ultimate parent of the marketplace group; incomplete relationship coding triggers schedule rejection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T106 Part B/C – Transaction schedules (purchases, sales, commissions, royalties, interest)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Monetary value of cross-border platform-service fees, technology/licence payments, management fees, and settlement flows with the related non-resident.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Aggregate values for each related party; the CRA compares these with the C$1M documentation threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Description of the tested party, arm's-length method (CUP / resale price / cost plus / TNMM / profit split), comparability adjustments, and the resulting intercompany price.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a lightweight B2B marketplace operator, TNMM tested-party analysis on the Canadian distributor/operator is typical; attach the contemporaneous study summary.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete T106: information-return penalties under s.162(7) of C$25 per day per form (minimum C$100, maximum C$2,500) plus possible 10% transfer-pricing adjustment penalty under s.247(3) if the CRA must make a transfer-pricing adjustment and documentation is inadequate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T1135 Foreign Income Verification Statement (filed with the T2, via CRA electronic filing).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the same date as the T2 (6 months after fiscal year-end); an extension to 12 months is available on CRA consent for a T1135 filed with the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T1135 Part A – Specific foreign property (bank accounts, foreign shares, loans, trust interests)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fair market value and cost of specified foreign property held by the Canadian corporation in excess of C$100,000 at any time in the year (e.g., Alibaba (Alipay) digital settlement balances held outside Canada, foreign e-wallet receivables).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An Alberta corporation owned by a non-resident reports foreign property even if the owners live in China; waivers do not exempt the corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T1135 Part C – Foreign affiliate shares and indebtedness
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Details of shareholdings in any foreign affiliate (e.g., Chinese logistics subsidiary) and intercompany balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the affiliate is controlled, Schedule T1134 must also be filed; base-erosion loans to the China parent are reportable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: s.162(7.01): late filing penalty of C$25 per day (C$100 minimum, C$2,500 maximum); where the failure continues for 24+ months, the penalty is C$500 per month of the late period up to a maximum C$12,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: GST/HST Return (Form GST34) + Marketplace/Facilitator rules under ETA s.273/CAN online GST/HST account (the platform is deemed the supplier for GST/HST on Canadian-measured taxable sales facilitated through the portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Monthly or quarterly, depending on taxable supplies; deadline one month after the reporting period end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Payment and return due at the end of the month following each GST/HST reporting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable supplies (B2B wholesale commissions, platform fees) measured for GST/HST at 5% (Alberta) or the provincial rate where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The platform operator is deemed to make and receive taxable supplies (ETA s.273.1 / s.273.3) for non-resident vendors; a non-resident corporate owner must register for the simplified GST/HST regime if it has C$30,000+ of Canadian-source revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: GST34 – Line 103/104 (tax collected) and Line 108 (input tax credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: GST/HST collected on commissions and ITCs for related expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident operators can claim ITCs in respect of Canadian purchases once registered; failure to collect = full tax liability plus penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Unregistered/undercollected GST/HST: the CRA assesses the deemed supplier for the tax not collected, plus arrears interest and a 6% penalty on the net tax balance (repeated failures: faster penalty escalation); director liability attaches for unremitted GST (ETA s.323).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory Part XIII withholding tax (ITA s.212(2)) on dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to a non-resident shareholder; a lower treaty rate must be proven before the payment is made or the excess can only be recovered by filing a Canadian non-resident tax return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Under the Canada–China Income Tax Agreement (1986, as amended), dividends paid to a Chinese-resident company that is the beneficial owner are taxable at 10% if the beneficial owner holds at least 10% of the voting power in the Canadian payer (15% otherwise). Administrative protocol: (1) the Chinese shareholder obtains a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the State Taxation Administration of China for the relevant calendar year; (2) the Canadian payer completes and retains CRA Form NR301 (or a treaty residency declaration containing the same information) with the TRC before remitting the dividend; (3) the payer withholds at the treaty rate (10% or 15%) only on the strength of the completed declaration and TRC; (4) if 25% was withheld at source, the shareholder recovers the excess by filing Form NR7-R (Application for Refund of Non-Resident Tax Withheld) with the CRA within two years of the end of the calendar year in which the tax was remitted; (5) supporting substance documentation (board minutes, beneficial-ownership analysis) must be retained because Canada applies GAAR (s.245) and beneficial-ownership tests to deny treaty relief where the Chinese recipient is a conduit/shell.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rates: 25% on interest (s.212(1)(b)) and 25% on royalties (s.212(1)(d)). Canada–China treaty rates: interest 10% (with a 10% rate for most interest flows; domestic arm's-length interest exemption may apply where the interest is fully taxable in China) and royalties 10% for payments for the use of copyrights, patents, trademarks, plans, secret formulas or processes, or industrial/airport/railway equipment. Participating debt-financing interest paid to a Chinese shareholder in a thinly capitalized structure is subject to the statutory/treaty rate plus re-characterization risk under s.247 and GAAR.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: C$1,000,000 — aggregate value of all non-arm's length cross-border transactions with the related non-resident in the fiscal period (including platform-service fees, intercompany commissions, royalty and interest flows) triggers the s.247(4) requirement to prepare and, upon CRA request, provide contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation. A Master File and Country-by-Country (CbC) report are required where the MNE group's consolidated revenue reaches the C$750M (€750M-equivalent) CbC reporting threshold; for the typical B2B marketplace operator below that threshold, the Local File / T106 documentation set is the controlling obligation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not apply a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations statute, but an equally binding substantive-equivalence regime operates through: (1) ITA s.245 GAAR, which denies tax benefits arising from avoidance transactions lacking bona fide economic substance/subjective purpose; (2) ITA s.247(2), permitting the CRA to re-price or re-characterize intercompany transactions that do not reflect what arm's-length parties would have agreed (substance over form); (3) common-law sham/agency doctrine, which can collapse a hollow Alberta corporation into its Chinese parent; and (4) case-law beneficial-ownership and LOB-style analysis under the Canada–China DTA, refusing treaty protection to shell recipients with no direction/disposition of the income. The Alberta corporation should maintain a physical head office, employees in Alberta, real board meetings, active bank management, and contractual ownership of the platform's Canadian customer contracts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of B2B marketplace commission revenue, false deduction of personal expenses, omitted Alipay/SWIFT wire settlements, or false books while filing the Alberta/federal T2.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ITA s.239(1) criminal conviction — on summary conviction, a fine of 50%–200% of the tax sought to be evaded and/or imprisonment of up to 2 years; on indictment, a fine of 100%–200% of the tax sought to be evaded and/or imprisonment of up to 5 years. Civil gross-negligence penalty under s.163(2) of 50% of the understated tax is applied as an alternative or in addition to interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who participate in or authorize the false return are personally prosecuted (imprisonment terms apply to individuals). The CRA can also pierce the corporate veil where the company was used as a sham, and directors are jointly and severally liable for the corporation's unremitted source deductions and GST/HST (s.227.1 / ETA s.323) even without intent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file / chronic late filing (T2, T106, T1135, GST/HST)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-filing of the T2 within 6 months of the fiscal year-end, failure to remit the balance due within the 2/3-month window, omitted T106 schedules for China-related-party flows, or recurrently late GST/HST returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: T2 late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month (max 12 months), doubled (10% + 2%/month, max 20 months) for a repeat failure within 3 years; daily compounding arrears interest at the CRA prescribed rate (base T-bill rate + 4%); T1135 information penalty of C$25/day (up to C$2,500, rising to C$12,000 for 24-month+ defaults); T106 penalty of C$25/day per form (up to C$2,500).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of an insolvent company are assessable under s.227.1 for source deductions and under ETA s.323 for GST/HST remittances (a director used as a shield cannot avoid liability). A travel/criminal-hold risk arises where the CRA commences a tax evasion inquiry alongside the civil assessments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Retaining C$1M+ of intra-group platform fees, management fees, royalties, and intercompany loans without contemporaneous s.247(4) documentation, or pricing the Canadian marketplace operator's services at a non-arm's-length margin (e.g., leaving zero taxable profit in Alberta).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: s.247(3) penalty equal to 10% of the net transfer-pricing adjustment (applied where the adjustment exceeds the greater of C$5,000 and 10% of the taxpayer's gross revenue, and the taxpayer failed to make reasonable efforts/documented positions); full tax reassessment at the 23% combined rate plus arrears interest; non-deductibility of 'unreasonable' intercompany charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed an intercompany invoice scheme that artificially relocated Alberta profit expose themselves to s.239 criminal prosecution if the understatement is deliberate; civil director liability can arise for unlawful distributions made after the company became unable to pay its tax debt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / artificial interposition / GAAR abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Alberta corporation as a hollow letterbox (no office, no employees, no bank decision-making) to route Chinese platform margin out of Canada, claim treaty benefits via a Chinese intermediary, or manufacture an SBD entitlement by splitting associated CCPCs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR (s.245) denies the abused tax benefit (SBD, treaty relief, loss utilization) and allows reassessment without a limitation-period extension (the 'avoidance transaction' standard); the CRA may also collapse the shell as an agent/sham under common law, and a s.247 re-characterization can impute revenue directly to the platform principal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the veil where the corporation is a mere agent/shadow of the Chinese parent; directors of the shell face civil restitution for diverted corporate opportunities and are exposed to the penalties described for tax evasion where the interposition was known and intended to deceive the CRA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / FINTRAC non-compliance in cross-border payment rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating Alibaba Pay (Alipay) and SWIFT wire settlement rails for B2B marketplace clients without a FINTRAC AML/CFT compliance program, failing to report EFTs and large cash/electronic fund transfers of C$10,000+, or acting as a funds transmitter/MSB without registration if the platform controls client funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PCMLTFA administrative monetary penalties (FINTRAC) of up to C$500,000 per violation for corporations (and C$1M+ for repeat/aggravated violations); Criminal Code s.462.31 laundering-of-proceeds offence: on indictment, imprisonment up to 10 years and fines at the court's discretion for the corporation; failure to register as a money services business in a province where applicable attracts separate provincial enforcement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: FINTRAC holds directors/officers to a 'reasonable measures' standard; the responsible AML compliance officer can be personally named in enforcement actions, and deliberate failure to report suspicious transactions can trigger personal criminal liability (up to 10 years in prison) for officers directing the conduct.
